audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel chapter 24, first-pass restored draft
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for cave setting and bodily euphemism, numerical power imbalance, providential interpretation by David's men, robe cutting, conscience, restraint of followers, anointed-language misuse, self-lowering rhetoric, Saul's remorse, dynastic oath, boundaries, and non-reconciliation.

verses.restored: When Saul returned from after Philistines, they told him, saying, Look, David is in wilderness of En-gedi.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Saul was returned from following the Philistines, that it was told him, saying, Behold, David is in the wilderness of Engedi.

modern.text: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁ֣ב שָׁא֔וּל מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי

verses.restored: Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men upon faces of Rocks of Wild Goats.

familiar.text: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats.

modern.text: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח שָׁא֗וּל שְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ בָּח֖וּר מִכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ אֶת דָּוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו עַל פְּנֵ֖י צוּרֵ֥י הַיְּעֵלִֽים

verses.restored: He came to sheepfolds by road, and a cave was there. Saul entered to cover his feet. David and his men were sitting in recesses of cave.

familiar.text: And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.

modern.text: Soon Saul came to the sheepfolds along the road, where there was a cave, and he went in to relieve himself. And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.

original.text: וַ֠יָּבֹא אֶל גִּדְר֨וֹת הַצֹּ֤אן עַל הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ וְשָׁ֣ם מְעָרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א שָׁא֖וּל לְהָסֵ֣ךְ אֶת רַגְלָ֑יו וְדָוִד֙ וַאֲנָשָׁ֔יו בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמְּעָרָ֖ה יֹשְׁבִֽים

verses.restored: Men of David said to him, Look, this is day of which YHWH said to you, Look, I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as good in your eyes. David arose and secretly cut off edge of robe belonging to Saul.

familiar.text: And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the LORD said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily.

modern.text: So David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do with him as you wish.’” Then David crept up secretly and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י דָוִ֜ד אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה הַיּ֜וֹם אֲֽשֶׁר אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֣ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י נֹתֵ֤ן אֶת איביך בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יִטַ֣ב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיִּכְרֹ֛ת אֶת כְּנַֽף הַמְּעִ֥יל אֲשֶׁר לְשָׁא֖וּל בַּלָּֽט

verses.restored: Afterward David's heart struck him because he had cut off edge belonging to Saul.

familiar.text: And it came to pass afterward, that David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.

modern.text: Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֥ךְ לֵב דָּוִ֖ד אֹת֑וֹ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֔ת אֶת כָּנָ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְשָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: He said to his men, Far be it from me by YHWH that I should do this thing to my lord, anointed of YHWH, to stretch out my hand against him, because he is anointed of YHWH.

familiar.text: And he said unto his men, The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD’s anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the LORD.

modern.text: So he said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed. May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו חָלִ֧ילָה לִּ֣י מֵֽיהוָ֗ה אִם אֶעֱשֶׂה֩ אֶת הַדָּבָ֨ר הַזֶּ֤ה לַֽאדֹנִי֙ לִמְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה לִשְׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא

verses.restored: David tore apart/restrained his men with these words and did not permit them to arise against Saul. Saul rose from cave and went on road.

familiar.text: So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul. But Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.

modern.text: With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and went on his way.

original.text: וַיְשַׁסַּ֨ע דָּוִ֤ד אֶת אֲנָשָׁיו֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א נְתָנָ֖ם לָק֣וּם אֶל שָׁא֑וּל וְשָׁא֛וּל קָ֥ם מֵהַמְּעָרָ֖ה וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ

verses.restored: Afterward David arose, went out from cave, and called after Saul, saying, My lord the king! Saul looked behind him, and David bowed with face to ground and prostrated himself.

familiar.text: David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David stooped with his face to the earth, and bowed himself.

modern.text: After that, David got up, went out of the cave, and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!” When Saul looked behind him, David bowed facedown in reverence

original.text: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד אַחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן וַיֵּצֵא֙ מן המערה וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַֽחֲרֵי שָׁא֛וּל לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּבֵּ֤ט שָׁאוּל֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּקֹּ֨ד דָּוִ֥ד אַפַּ֛יִם אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: David said to Saul, Why do you hear words of humans saying, Look, David seeks your harm?

familiar.text: And David said to Saul, Wherefore hearest thou men’s words, saying, Behold, David seeketh thy hurt?

modern.text: and said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’?

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ לְשָׁא֔וּל לָ֧מָּה תִשְׁמַ֛ע אֶת דִּבְרֵ֥י אָדָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ רָעָתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Look, this day your eyes have seen that YHWH gave you today into my hand in cave. One said to kill you, but there was pity upon you, and I said, I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, because he is anointed of YHWH.

familiar.text: Behold, this day thine eyes have seen how that the LORD had delivered thee to day into mine hand in the cave: and some bade me kill thee: but mine eye spared thee; and I said, I will not put forth mine hand against my lord; for he is the LORD’s anointed.

modern.text: Behold, this day you have seen with your own eyes that the LORD delivered you into my hand in the cave. I was told to kill you, but I spared you and said, ‘I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed.’

original.text: הִנֵּה֩ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה רָא֣וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר נְתָנְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה הַיּ֤וֹם בְּיָדִי֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וְאָמַ֥ר לַהֲרָגֲךָ֖ וַתָּ֣חָס עָלֶ֑יךָ וָאֹמַ֗ר לֹא אֶשְׁלַ֤ח יָדִי֙ בַּֽאדֹנִ֔י כִּי מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא

verses.restored: My father, see, yes, see edge of your robe in my hand. For in that I cut off edge of your robe and did not kill you, know and see there is no evil or rebellion in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt my life to take it.

familiar.text: Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, know thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in mine hand, and I have not sinned against thee; yet thou huntest my soul to take it.

modern.text: See, my father, look at the corner of your robe in my hand. For I cut it off, but I did not kill you. See and know that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands. I have not sinned against you, even though you are hunting me down to take my life.

original.text: וְאָבִ֣י רְאֵ֔ה גַּ֗ם רְאֵ֛ה אֶת כְּנַ֥ף מְעִילְךָ֖ בְּיָדִ֑י כִּ֡י בְּכָרְתִי֩ אֶת כְּנַ֨ף מְעִֽילְךָ֜ וְלֹ֣א הֲרַגְתִּ֗יךָ דַּ֤ע וּרְאֵה֙ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין בְּיָדִ֜י רָעָ֤ה וָפֶ֨שַׁע֙ וְלֹא חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֛ה צֹדֶ֥ה אֶת נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ

verses.restored: May YHWH judge between me and you, and may YHWH avenge me from you, but my hand shall not be against you.

familiar.text: The LORD judge between me and thee, and the LORD avenge me of thee: but mine hand shall not be upon thee.

modern.text: May the LORD judge between you and me, and may the LORD take vengeance on you, but my hand will never be against you.

original.text: יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט יְהוָה֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּנְקָמַ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑ךָּ וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה בָּֽךְ

modern.text: As the old proverb says, ‘Wickedness proceeds from the wicked.’ But my hand will never be against you.

original.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֹאמַ֗ר מְשַׁל֙ הַקַּדְמֹנִ֔י מֵרְשָׁעִ֖ים יֵ֣צֵא רֶ֑שַׁע וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה בָּֽךְ

verses.restored: After whom has king of Israel gone out? After whom are you pursuing? After a dead dog, after one flea?

familiar.text: After whom is the king of Israel come out? after whom dost thou pursue? after a dead dog, after a flea.

modern.text: Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?

original.text: אַחֲרֵ֨י מִ֤י יָצָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֥י מִ֖י אַתָּ֣ה רֹדֵ֑ף אַֽחֲרֵי֙ כֶּ֣לֶב מֵ֔ת אַחֲרֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֥שׁ אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: May YHWH be judge and judge between me and you. May he see and contend my case and judge me from your hand.

familiar.text: The LORD therefore be judge, and judge between me and thee, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of thine hand.

modern.text: May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me. May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand.” David’s Oath to Saul

original.text: וְהָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְדַיָּ֔ן וְשָׁפַ֖ט בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְיֵ֨רֶא֙ וְיָרֵ֣ב אֶת רִיבִ֔י וְיִשְׁפְּטֵ֖נִי מִיָּדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: When David finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, Is this your voice, my son David? Saul lifted his voice and wept.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when David had made an end of speaking these words unto Saul, that Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.

modern.text: When David had finished saying these things, Saul called back, “Is that your voice, David my son?” Then Saul wept aloud

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י כְּכַלּ֣וֹת דָּוִ֗ד לְדַבֵּ֞ר אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל הֲקֹלְךָ֥ זֶ֖ה בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיִּשָּׂ֥א שָׁא֛וּל קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ

familiar.text: And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.

modern.text: and said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, though I have rewarded you with evil.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד צַדִּ֥יק אַתָּ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ גְּמַלְתַּ֣נִי הַטּוֹבָ֔ה וַאֲנִ֖י גְּמַלְתִּ֥יךָ הָרָעָֽה

familiar.text: And thou hast shewed this day how that thou hast dealt well with me: forasmuch as when the LORD had delivered me into thine hand, thou killedst me not.

modern.text: And you have shown this day how well you have dealt with me; for when the LORD delivered me into your hand, you did not kill me.

original.text: ואת הִגַּ֣דְתָּ הַיּ֔וֹם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֥יתָה אִתִּ֖י טוֹבָ֑ה אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר סִגְּרַ֧נִי יְהוָ֛ה בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א הֲרַגְתָּֽנִי

modern.text: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go away unharmed? May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me this day.

modern.text: Now I know for sure that you will be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י מָלֹ֖ךְ תִּמְל֑וֹךְ וְקָ֨מָה֙ בְּיָ֣דְךָ֔ מַמְלֶ֖כֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Now swear to me by YHWH that you will not cut off my seed after me and will not destroy my name from house of my father.

modern.text: So now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father’s house.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֤בְעָה לִּי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה אִם תַּכְרִ֥ית אֶת זַרְעִ֖י אַֽחֲרָ֑י וְאִם תַּשְׁמִ֥יד אֶת שְׁמִ֖י מִבֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי

verses.restored: David swore to Saul. Saul went to his house, and David and his men went up to stronghold.

familiar.text: And David sware unto Saul. And Saul went home; but David and his men gat them up unto the hold.

modern.text: So David gave his oath to Saul. Then Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֥ע דָּוִ֖ד לְשָׁא֑וּל וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל בֵּית֔וֹ וְדָוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו עָל֖וּ עַל הַמְּצוּדָֽה

translation_notes: Saul brings three thousand chosen men against a much smaller fugitive community. The power imbalance remains even when he is briefly vulnerable in the cave.
'Cover his feet' is a bodily euphemism for relieving himself. The scene should not be sexualized or used to shame ordinary bodily functions.
David's men interpret opportunity as Divine authorization. Group certainty and providential language do not make killing morally required.
Cutting the robe may carry symbolic royal meaning as well as proof of proximity. David's conscience responds even to a nonlethal violation.
David refuses to kill Saul and restrains his men. This is a significant rejection of assassination and retaliation, not proof that abused people must stay close to abusers.
'Anointed of YHWH' limits David's action in this scene but cannot establish royal impunity, immunity from removal, or a ban on lawful accountability.
David bows and calls Saul father/king while pleading his case. Survival deference under power should not be confused with free consent or endorsement.
David calls himself a dead dog and flea. These are self-lowering rhetorical images, not permission for dehumanizing language or low-self-worth spirituality.
Saul's tears, confession, blessing, and recognition may be sincere in the moment, but remorse without durable changed behavior does not automatically restore safety.
David does not return home with Saul; he returns to the stronghold. Forgiveness, mercy, or nonretaliation do not require reconciliation, trust, proximity, or removal of boundaries.
Saul's request about descendants reflects ancient dynastic violence. The oath does not erase later political complexity.
safety_note: Do not turn David's mercy into a command that survivors remain with violent people, surrender boundaries, or accept tears as proof of lasting change. Saul is still an armed king pursuing fugitives. 'Do not touch the anointed' cannot shield rulers, clergy, or charismatic leaders from investigation, removal, restraint, or justice. The chapter rejects assassination, but it does not demand passivity, reconciliation, or institutional impunity.
